docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
I am a Remote Sensing and GIS professional with experience in geospatial analysis, agricultural remote sensing, drone image processing, machine learning, and WebGIS development. Currently, I work as a Young Professional-II (Remote Sensing & GIS) at ICAR–Indian Agricultural Statistics Research Institute (ICAR-IASRI), New Delhi, where I contribute to national research projects involving agricultural monitoring, geospatial analytics, and spatial data management.

My expertise includes GIS analysis, satellite image processing, drone data processing, spatial modelling, climate data analysis, Google Earth Engine, Python automation, and machine learning for geospatial applications. I enjoy transforming complex spatial datasets into meaningful insights that support decision-making in agriculture, water resources, and environmental management.

My research interests include precision agriculture, groundwater recharge mapping, climate change, crop monitoring, environmental modelling, and GeoAI. I am passionate about building innovative geospatial solutions that bridge research with real-world applications.

docs.text:
January 2024 – February 2025 | New Delhi, India

Project: National Mission for Sustaining Himalayan Ecosystems (NMSHE)

Key Responsibilities

  • Mapped Groundwater Recharge Potential Zones in Uttarakhand, India, using Multi-Criteria Decision-Making techniques such as AHP and ANP, as well as machine learning techniques like Random Forest and XGBoost. Conducted research on groundwater recharge potential zones and surface water changes in the Indian Himalayas, assessing how climate variability impacts regional water resources.
  • Analyzed climate scenarios and their effects on forest cover and agriculture in mountainous regions, focusing on temperature fluctuations, precipitation patterns, and extreme weather events Heatwaves and cold waves to inform climate adaptation strategies.
  • Utilized Google Earth Engine, Python, and ArcMap to process and visualize extensive geospatial datasets, developing tools to support climate resilience in agricultural systems.
  • Developed a comprehensive database for agricultural contingency planning across India with ICAR-CRIDA data, including cropping plans to guide climate-sensitive agriculture.
  • Regridded tmin, tmax, and rainfall data from the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) to ensure spatial consistency for advanced climate analysis.
  • Georeferenced and digitized local governance data from the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, creating a nationwide database for integrated climate and resource management.
  • Generated scripts for SPI (Standardized Precipitation Index) and SPEI (Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index) calculations to assess drought risk and water stress levels, enhancing understanding of water variability, climate impacts, and agricultural productivity across regions.
  • Mapping well locations for groundwater research and analyzing Census data to map tribal demographics.
  • Collaborating with NMSHE and NICRA teams, providing essential geospatial datasets.
  • Built and maintained project geodatabases, ensuring proper metadata, naming conventions, and directory structure.
  • Produced high-quality thematic maps, figures, and charts for technical reports and research publications.
  • Conducted QA/QC checks to ensure spatial accuracy and data integrity.

from pathlib import Path
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Main 30DayMap folder
# ---------------------------------------------------------
base = Path(r"D:\30_day_map\day_1")

# Delhi boundary
boundary_path = base / "delhi_bound.shp"

# Output folder for Day 01
output = base / "Day01_points"
output.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Find possible OSM POI shapefiles automatically
# ---------------------------------------------------------
poi_files = []

for shp in base.rglob("*.shp"):

    name = shp.name.lower()

    if "poi" in name:
        poi_files.append(shp)

print("=" * 65)
print("POSSIBLE POI FILES")
print("=" * 65)

if len(poi_files) == 0:
    print("No POI shapefile found.")
else:
    for i, path in enumerate(poi_files, start=1):
        print(f"{i}. {path}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Select likely OSM POI file
# ---------------------------------------------------------
preferred = [
    p for p in poi_files
    if "gis_osm_pois" in p.name.lower()
]

if preferred:
    poi_path = preferred[0]

elif poi_files:
    poi_path = poi_files[0]

else:
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "No POI shapefile was found inside the 30DaysMap folder."
    )

print("\nSelected POI file:")
print(poi_path)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Read data
# ---------------------------------------------------------
pois = gpd.read_file(poi_path)
delhi = gpd.read_file(boundary_path)

print("\n" + "=" * 65)
print("DELHI POI DATA")
print("=" * 65)

print("Features :", len(pois))
print("CRS      :", pois.crs)
print("Geometry :")
print(pois.geom_type.value_counts())

print("\nFields:")
print(list(pois.columns))

print("\nFirst 5 records:")
print(pois.head().to_string())

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Inspect useful categorical fields
# ---------------------------------------------------------
possible_fields = [
    "fclass",
    "type",
    "amenity",
    "name",
    "code"
]

print("\n" + "=" * 65)
print("CATEGORY CHECK")
print("=" * 65)

for field in possible_fields:

    if field in pois.columns:

        print(f"\nFIELD: {field}")
        print("-" * 40)

        print(
            pois[field]
            .fillna("NULL")
            .value_counts()
            .head(30)
            .to_string()
        )

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Boundary information
# ---------------------------------------------------------
print("\n" + "=" * 65)
print("DELHI BOUNDARY")
print("=" * 65)

print("Features :", len(delhi))
print("CRS      :", delhi.crs)
print("Bounds   :", delhi.total_bounds)

# Match CRS
if pois.crs != delhi.crs:
    pois = pois.to_crs(delhi.crs)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Keep only POIs inside Delhi
# ---------------------------------------------------------
delhi_geom = delhi.geometry.union_all()

pois_delhi = pois[
    pois.geometry.intersects(delhi_geom)
].copy()

print("\nPOIs before Delhi filter :", len(pois))
print("POIs inside Delhi        :", len(pois_delhi))

# Save cleaned Day 30 working data
clean_path = output / "Delhi_POI_Day1.gpkg"

pois_delhi.to_file(
    clean_path,
    layer="poi",
    driver="GPKG"
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Simple DAY 1-style baseline preview
# ---------------------------------------------------------
fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(9, 10),
    facecolor="white"
)

delhi.plot(
    ax=ax,
    facecolor="#F2F2F2",
    edgecolor="black",
    linewidth=1
)

pois_delhi.plot(
    ax=ax,
    markersize=2,
    alpha=0.55
)

ax.set_title(
    "DELHI POINTS OF INTEREST\nDay 1 Baseline",
    fontsize=17,
    weight="bold",
    pad=15
)

ax.set_axis_off()

plt.tight_layout()

preview_path = output / "Step1_Day1_POI_Baseline.png"

plt.savefig(
    preview_path,
    dpi=300,
    bbox_inches="tight",
    facecolor="white"
)

plt.show()

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Final summary
# ---------------------------------------------------------
print("\n" + "=" * 65)
print("STEP 1 COMPLETE")
print("=" * 65)

print("\nWorking POI dataset:")
print(clean_path)

print("\nBaseline preview:")
print(preview_path)

from pathlib import Path
import geopandas as gpd
import folium
from folium.plugins import Fullscreen, MousePosition


# =========================================================
# 1. PATHS + DATA
# =========================================================

base = Path(r"D:\30_day_map\day_1")
output = base / "Day01_points"

poi_path = output / "Delhi_POI_Classified.gpkg"
boundary_path = base / "delhi_bound.shp"

html_path = output / "Day1_A Spatial Portrait of Delhi.html"

pois = gpd.read_file(poi_path).to_crs("EPSG:4326")
delhi = gpd.read_file(boundary_path).to_crs("EPSG:4326")

print("POIs       :", f"{len(pois):,}")
print("Categories :", pois["category"].nunique())


# =========================================================
# 2. CATEGORY STYLING

    "Parks & Recreation": {
        "color": "#4D9D68",
        "radius": 2.2,
        "opacity": 0.38
    },

    "Education": {
        "color": "#55B7E8",
        "radius": 3.3,
        "opacity": 0.85
    },

    "Health": {
        "color": "#FF6268",
        "radius": 4.2,
        "opacity": 0.95
    },

    "Food & Drink": {
        "color": "#FFB454",
        "radius": 3.8,
        "opacity": 0.92
    },

    "Shopping": {
        "color": "#CF83ED",
        "radius": 3.8,
        "opacity": 0.92
    },

    "Tourism & Heritage": {
        "color": "#F3D267",
        "radius": 3.8,
        "opacity": 0.94
    },

    "Public Services": {
        "color": "#68D2C3",
        "radius": 3.2,
        "opacity": 0.85
    },

    "Urban Infrastructure": {
        "color": "#9BA7AD",
        "radius": 2.7,
        "opacity": 0.55
    },

    "Other": {
        "color": "#53616A",
        "radius": 1.8,
        "opacity": 0.25
    }
}

# 3. CREATE DARK INTERACTIVE MAP
# =========================================================

    location=[28.65, 77.15],
    zoom_start=10,
    tiles=None,
    control_scale=True,
    prefer_canvas=True
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Esri Dark Gray
# ---------------------------------------------------------

folium.TileLayer(
    tiles=(
        "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/"
        "Canvas/World_Dark_Gray_Base/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}"
    ),
    attr="Esri",
    name="Dark Gray",
    overlay=False,
    control=True,
    show=True
).add_to(m)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Optional imagery
# ---------------------------------------------------------

folium.TileLayer(
    tiles=(
        "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/"
        "World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}"
    ),
    attr="Esri",
    name="Satellite",
    overlay=False,
    control=True,
    show=False
).add_to(m)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Delhi boundary
# ---------------------------------------------------------

folium.GeoJson(
    delhi.__geo_interface__,
    name="Delhi Boundary",

    style_function=lambda feature: {
        "fillColor": "#071016",
        "color": "#87969E",
        "weight": 1.4,
        "fillOpacity": 0.08
    }
).add_to(m)

# 4. ADD INTERACTIVE POI CONSTELLATIONS
# =========================================================

category_order = [
    "Parks & Recreation",
    "Education",
    "Health",
    "Food & Drink",
    "Shopping",
    "Tourism & Heritage",
    "Public Services",
    "Urban Infrastructure",
    "Other"
]


for category in category_order:

    subset = pois[
        pois["category"] == category
    ]

    if len(subset) == 0:
        continue

    style = styles[category]

    group = folium.FeatureGroup(
        name=f"{category} ({len(subset):,})",
        show=True
    )

    for _, row in subset.iterrows():

        geom = row.geometry

        if geom is None or geom.is_empty:
            continue

        lat = geom.y
        lon = geom.x

        # ---------------------------------------------
        # Popup values
        # ---------------------------------------------

        name = row.get("name", None)
        fclass = row.get("fclass", "")
        osm_id = row.get("osm_id", "")

        if name is None or str(name).lower() in [
            "nan", "none", ""
        ]:
            name = "Unnamed place"

        popup_html = f"""
        <div style="
            font-family:Arial,sans-serif;
            min-width:190px;
        ">

        <div style="
            font-size:14px;
            font-weight:bold;
            margin-bottom:7px;
        ">
            {name}
        </div>

        <table style="
            font-size:11px;
            line-height:1.5;
        ">

        <tr>
            <td><b>Category</b></td>
            <td style="padding-left:10px;">
                {category}
            </td>
        </tr>

        <tr>
            <td><b>OSM class</b></td>
            <td style="padding-left:10px;">
                {fclass}
            </td>
        </tr>

        <tr>
            <td><b>OSM ID</b></td>
            <td style="padding-left:10px;">
                {osm_id}
            </td>
        </tr>

        </table>

        </div>
        """

        # POI symbol
        # ---------------------------------------------

        folium.CircleMarker(
            location=[lat, lon],

            radius=style["radius"],

            color=style["color"],

            weight=0.5,

            opacity=style["opacity"],

            fill=True,

            fill_color=style["color"],

            fill_opacity=style["opacity"],

            tooltip=f"{name} • {category}",

            popup=folium.Popup(
                popup_html,
                max_width=280
            )
        ).add_to(group)

    group.add_to(m)

    location=[28.6139, 77.2090],

    icon=folium.DivIcon(

<div style="

</div>

<div style="
    color:#D9C58F;
    font-size:8px;
    margin-top:9px;
    letter-spacing:1px;
">
    DAY 1 • Points
</div>

</div>
"""

m.get_root().html.add_child(
    folium.Element(title_html)
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------

legend_items = ""

for category in category_order[:-1]:

    color = styles[category]["color"]

    legend_items += f"""

m.get_root().html.add_child(

Fullscreen(
    position="topright",
    title="Fullscreen",
    title_cancel="Exit fullscreen",
    force_separate_button=True
).add_to(m)

MousePosition(

# Fit precisely around Delhi
m.fit_bounds([

m.save(str(html_path))

This project explores Delhi through its mapped points of interest, illustrating how location-based data can represent the city's public services, amenities, and urban destinations. The map uses a dark cartographic background with selective colours to distinguish POI categories and improve visual contrast.
